items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: I played with, as I said, Clark Terry, I worked with him, played with him

ctx.x: Yes. Practice every day and I find that it pays off. Now, I get through working, say, 11:00 o'clock I breakneck home, get home and go to sleep. Then I wake up early, turn my records on, and listen to all these programs, jazz, and I want to hear who's playing something. And -- you see I was thrown in -- my whole life I had a list of the trumpet players that I've played with, it would take maybe three or four hours to name the trumpet players I've played with. From Joe Smith, to Rex Stewart, to the trumpet player…

them all night long. But I listened to these guys, they all had something great about them. About their playing, so I wanted to be able to play with them and I did play with them and last -- night before last I played with, as I said, Clark Terry, I worked with him, played with him and the night before last I was at a seminar, I played with Thad Jones and Jimmy Owens. Now we had -- went on individually, we gave our history of what we're playing and our style of playing and so we did solo play, like I preached on…

They said bring the boy that preaches, so I'd go out on a job and preach with a plunger and a mute and I put a hat on my head, some specs and I had a book like it was a bible, and that was the act that I had. And they would have me preaching. They thought that was great in Nashville, in those days. So I learned to do that. And I demonstrated that that over there the other night, about preaching and I showed them how it's done and all that stuff and then up to date -- I told them -- my style of trumpet playing, I…
